precepts.text: That's why Paul told Timothy, let no man despise your youth.
precepts.point: A brother: Good point behind that. That's why Paul told Timothy, let no man despise your youth. Because God chose that man, Timothy, at that point, and he's going to be over some older men in age. And it doesn't make the older man less. But don't try to use your age and your worldly wisdom to think it's going to outshine God's wisdom. God's going to choose who he wants and where he wants them in his body. And that's just what it is. Just be glad that you part of this mission, and play your role.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
That is why Paul told Timothy, let no man despise your youth. God chose that man, Timothy, at that point, and he was going to be over some men older than him in age.

It doesn't make the older man less. But don't try to use your age and your worldly wisdom as though it is going to outshine God's wisdom. God is going to choose who he wants and where he wants them in his body, and that is just what it is. Be glad that you are part of this mission, and play your role.

It fits what Sirach 34 says: “The law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth.” Wisdom is in the law and the faithful mouth, not in the gray hair. A young man who knows God's laws, keeps them and labors in them, teaching all them that seek learning, is not to be despised because of his youth; and an older man who never learned the law is still an infant, however many years he has.

precepts.text: In the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits. A seducing spirit looks like it is good for you, but it is going to destroy you; like drugs: that crack feels real good, but you are not able to see around you, and your whole life is being destroyed. That is why it is important to be studying, reading your four chapters, being around godly men and godly women, so somebody can have your back.
precepts.point: And sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death. It becomes action; that sin is the action you take after you have been enticed by your lust. And it always ends in destruction. That is why we have to be on point.
precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed means there is some attraction there, something that makes us gravitate toward the elements in us that cause us to sin. It seduces us: it looks like it is right for us, but it is not. Paul warned of it: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits.”

A seducing spirit looks like it is good for you, but it is going to destroy you. Like drugs: that crack feels real good to the crackhead, but he is not able to see around him, and his whole life is being destroyed.

The only way you are going to see whether it is good for you or not is by filtering it through the scriptures. That is why it is important to be studying, reading your four chapters, being around godly men and godly women, so somebody can have your back. You have to be in the spirit to discern whether a thing is righteousness or Satan’s kiss.

Temptation begins internally; the lust is in you. When temptation presents itself you begin to be drawn to it, sin starts enticing you, and it grows through agreement: you get enticed, then you agree with it. “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” It becomes action, and it always ends in destruction. “There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.” In your own counsel you will always think you are right, and that is how people give heed to seducing spirits and depart from the faith.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
The believers in Acts 4 “were of one heart and of one soul” and “had all things common”. To keep from losing ourselves, selling ourselves out and losing our souls, we have to grow the same way. Paul shows what pulls us away: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”.

The seducing spirits are money and wealth, the many things that distract us from God, from Christ and from our purpose in life. We live in an era where vanity is a drug and attention is a drug. At the blitz last week, kids said they want to be streamers. What about a plumber, a mechanic, a builder, an architect, a lawyer, an engineer, the things that actually build nations? That is why we have been destroyed as a people. And there are men and women in the faith who want to leave this and go to the world and stream.

The “doctrines of devils” are religion, man-made religion. “Speaking lies in hypocrisy” is politics: a lie that makes you feel assimilated into a government that is kicking you out of it. If you are Israel, what they call black, you cannot be in their government. There is one black governor in this whole country, and all the black generals have been taken out as not qualified. They are making their country great again in their eyes.

“Having their conscience seared with a hot iron.” Religion, politics and the gifts of this world sear the conscience. Money, riches and comfort should not be your god; the American dream is a lie. Having all things in common, in faith and understanding, is what keeps us from departing from the faith.

precepts.text: Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth. That is the truth these religions would have you depart from.
precepts.point: Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats: that is Roman Catholicism. They forbid the men to marry, and they command you to abstain from meats during Lent.

David says: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.”

God's law is the truth, and that is what these religions would have you depart from. We are in the latter times now. Some of you men and women listening will depart from the truth of Christ: some because of persecution for the word's sake, and some because you see signs and wonders, technological signs and wonders, and believe we have been wrong all this time. It is already written, as Christ said: “there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders”, and “Behold, I have told you before.”

They give heed to seducing spirits and doctrines of devils, “Speaking lies in hypocrisy”: they have the Bible, but they are hypocrites. The religion of the false prophet starts with Christianity.

But the law is the truth, and those who believe and know the truth receive with thanksgiving what God created, and do not depart from his everlasting righteousness.

Leviticus 11.

The Roman Catholic Church is the mother church of every Protestant denomination on the tree: Orthodox, Jehovah's Witness, Presbyterian, Lutheran, Methodist, Episcopalian, Mormon, Evangelical, Pentecostal, Baptist, Adventist, Anglican, all the way to Christian nationalism. precepts.text: Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine. Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery, the congregation.
precepts.point: His mouth commanded it and his spirit gathered them; he cast the lot for them and divided it unto them by line, as the land was divided: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and David got big portions, Obadiah, Micah, Amos, Jonah, and Nahum small ones. They shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation: we will possess the land for ever and the word of God for ever.
precepts.why:
Isaiah says “Seek ye out of the book of the Lord, and read”, and Paul tells Timothy the same thing: “Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.” Read, brothers and sisters. Give attendance to reading, to exhortation and to doctrine until Christ comes.

“Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery”: the presbytery is the congregation. Just as Timothy had the gift of the Holy Spirit within him, we all have the gift of the Holy Spirit within us. Don’t let anybody tell you that to show the gift you have to speak in tongues. John the Baptist had the gift of the Holy Spirit, anointed in his mother’s womb. Did John the Baptist speak in tongues? No. Stop listening to these Christians.

And what we read must be the book of the Lord alone. “none shall want her mate”: you cannot mate the Bible with any other book. Islam tries to do that, mixing the Quran with the Bible, and God says you cannot. “for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.” God’s mouth commanded these words to be written and his spirit gathered them together; “he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line”. As he divided the land of Israel by line, he gave the prophets lines to write: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel and David big portions, Obadiah, Micah, Amos, Jonah and Nahum small ones. “they shall possess it for ever”: as we will possess the land for ever, we will possess the word of God for ever, and we give attendance to reading it until he comes.

precepts.point: Verse 3 says meats are received with thanksgiving by them which believe and know the truth. The truth is the law, so the meat is sanctified by the word, not by a prayer over it.
precepts.why:
Christians take this chapter and say every creature is good to eat, so long as you pray over it. But Paul says the meats God created are “to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.” So what is the truth? “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The truth is the law.

That changes the whole verse. The meat is not received by everybody who bows his head over his plate. It is received by them that know the law. People say, just give thanks, just pray on it, and it's all right. Then can I pray on a human's foot and eat it? Pork carries the worm that lives in the muscle and can go to your brain; the shrimp, the lobster, the catfish and all the shellfish are bottom feeders whose job is to clean the ocean, the roaches of the sea. A prayer does not change what they are.

“For every creature of God is good” means what Genesis means: “God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good to serve its purpose. Worms prepare the land for planting, but we don't eat worms. The pig was the garbage disposal before there were trucks to pick up the garbage. Good for its work, not for your plate.

And Paul finishes: “For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” A Christian never reads up to that verse. The word of God is the law, the truth, and the law is what tells you which creatures are sanctified to eat. Many who have come into the truth, who know Christ is black and that we are Israel, are still struggling with that pork and that shrimp. This is the answer to that struggle: the ones who receive it with thanksgiving are those who know the law.

precepts.text: He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment.
precepts.point: Verse 3 says meats are received with thanksgiving by them which believe and know the truth. The truth is the law, so the meat is sanctified by the word, not by a prayer over it.
precepts.why:
Paul says the meats are received “of them which believe and know the truth.” What is it to believe? “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment”. If you take heed to the commandments, you believe. Does a Christian believe in the commandments? So when he says you can eat anything as long as you receive it with thanksgiving, no: you can pray all you want, but you don't believe and you don't know the truth. Those are the very things that can save your life.

Finish the verse: “and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” If you believe in the commandments and keep the dietary laws, will you be worrying about high blood pressure? Will you be worrying about a foot amputation because of diabetes, about high cholesterol, about gout that takes brothers' fingers and feet? No, because you are not eating in a way where those sicknesses can come your way. The law tells you the food you can eat and the food you cannot eat.

All of that comes because people wanted to eat nasty, dirty food the Lord said don't eat. So take heed to yourself. Believing is not a prayer said over the plate; it is taking heed to the commandment, and the one who does fares never the worse.

precepts.text: This is the law of the beasts, to make a difference between the unclean and the clean.
precepts.point: Verse 3 says meats are received with thanksgiving by them which believe and know the truth. The truth is the law, so the meat is sanctified by the word, not by a prayer over it.
precepts.why:
Paul says the meat “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” So where were the animals sanctified to be eaten or not to be eaten? In the law.

Leviticus 11 closes: “For I am the Lord your God: ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He repeats it: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” How do you become holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. To sanctify yourself and be holy you have to apply the law, the statutes and the commandments.

Then: “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.” This law takes in all the animals, whether they live on the earth or in the waters. That is how the word sanctifies the meat: by making a difference between what can be eaten and what cannot. Some animals are clean, some are unclean. It is basic.

The churches don't want you to learn the Old Testament, because they don't want you to be saved. “Keep my commandments, and live”. If you don't keep the law you are not going to live. John says “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food is sin; eating pork is going to kill you, and overeating is going to kill you.

You are supposed to be the temple of God. If you keep destroying yourself with the way you eat, you are working against what the Lord says, and against the work we are all called here to do. The meat that is received with thanksgiving is the meat the law sanctified.

precepts.text: Commanding to abstain from meats is a doctrine of devils; the creature is sanctified by the word of God, which is the dietary law.
precepts.point: Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Paul warns that “in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils”, among them “commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.” Commanding to abstain from meats is a doctrine of devils; the Most High gave meat to man here in Genesis 9:3.

But read the whole thing. “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving: For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God. The word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law, the law of the beasts that makes a difference between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not. So the doctrine that says you can pray over anything and eat it is itself the seducing spirit and doctrine of devils.

precepts.text: Every creature received with thanksgiving is sanctified by the word of God; the word of God sanctified the clean beasts of Leviticus 11.
precepts.point: The law perisheth not, but remaineth in his force; that law did not change at all. Do not let anybody confuse you, especially if you are new in the truth: eat what the Most High instructed you to eat.

note.label: Leviticus 11: The Dietary Law of Clean and Unclean Beasts

precepts.why:
Do not confuse yourself with 1 Timothy 4:4 and think you can eat whatever you want. Read it: “every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving: For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.”

It is sanctified by the word of God. So find what the word of God sanctified, and that is “the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth” in Leviticus 11. What is sanctified is what the Most High already made clean; Paul is not opening the door to the camel and the swine.

The Most High explained everything and then summed it up: “To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.” That difference is what the word of God sanctifies.
